title: Chain-encoding clauses stay local to their index
statement: Let $i$ be a natural number and let $ml$ be a lifting map sending each literal over a variable type $V$ to a literal over $\mathtt{AuxVar}\,V$, and suppose that $ml(l)$ is local to index $i$ for every literal $l$. Then, for every list of literals $\mathit{lits}$ over $V$ and every chain counter $j$, each $3$-clause occurring in the chain of clauses built from $\mathit{lits}$ (with clause index $i$, lifting map $ml$, and counter $j$) has all three of its literals local to index $i$.
hypotheses_covered: lifting map ml from literals over V to literals over AuxVar V
every ml(l) is local to index i
lits is an arbitrary list of literals over V
j is an arbitrary chain counter
c₃ is a 3-clause appearing in the built chain
replaced:
Every literal in any 3-clause produced by $\texttt{SATTo3SAT.buildChain}\,i\,ml\,\ldots$
is local to index $i$, provided the lifting map $ml$ itself produces only literals local
to $i$.
